summary: One high-confidence join defect changes the analytic sample; one suggestion.

findings.title: State join is many-to-many and duplicates workers

evidence.claim: The join duplicates worker rows because states.csv has two rows for S03.
evidence.found: The join declares no relationship, and the row count rises after it.
evidence.verified_by: Ran the build in a scratch copy: 500 rows before the join, 527 after.

findings.refutation: Looked for a distinct() or a row-count check after the join; there is none.
findings.explanation: Duplicated workers inflate every weighted mean and the regression N.
findings.fix: Add relationship = "many-to-one" and unmatched = "error" to the join, and deduplicate states.csv.

findings.title: Mean age ignores missing ages silently

evidence.claim: na.rm = TRUE drops six missing ages without reporting them.
evidence.found: mean(age, na.rm = TRUE) with no count of the dropped rows.

findings.fix: Report the number of missing ages beside the mean, or filter them explicitly first.

evidence.claim: The same .rds file is read in two places.

findings.title: Is the bootstrap meant to be reproducible?

evidence.claim: No seed is set before the bootstrap in the helper the script sources.
evidence.found: The helper was not in the reviewed files, so the seed could not be checked.
evidence.verified_by: Not determinable from the reviewed files.
